posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Spiff:

Quite a few people mention GSF's difficulty level.  Maybe we'll need to come up with an anti-Advanced rules houserule to make it fun for the casuals.

The game has a bunch of easy to turn nobs to adjust the difficulty. You can:

  1. Start the game with more/less ships deployed

  2. Add/Remove shields or weaponry to taste

  3. Start the game with +1W/+1D on your ship panel

In the PAX East demo (which, if anything, was critiqued for being almost too easy), we stacked the mission deck and did a combination of #1 and #2

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked: Just listened to Tom talking about GSF. I was really surprised how much he liked it despite the book keeping and difficulty. I mean, he really liked it it sounded like. Comparison to making Ghost Stories look like a cakewalk was hillarious and appropriate. Joel Eddy didn't win many games much squeeked out a win which is awesome. Joel's review really hit on a key point that I found profound. The tense nature of the game and that constant feeling of danger is really gonna scratch an itch for folks. I think thats what Joel liked most about it, and even though he didn't mention it specifically, I get the sense thats what is making Tom keep the game himself as well.
